facts.t: The 1996 Act is India's copy of a UN template
facts.d: It is built on the UNCITRAL Model Law, adopted so that foreign investors would meet a familiar dispute-resolution regime. The alignment was deliberate economic policy, arriving five years after liberalisation.

facts.t: One 2003 judgment undid much of the Act's purpose
facts.d: ONGC v. Saw Pipes read patent illegality into the public policy ground for setting aside awards. A statute designed to minimise judicial intervention acquired a wide new door into court — narrowed only by the 2015 amendment.

facts.t: The Arbitration Council of India still isn't fully functional
facts.d: Created by the 2019 amendment to promote institutional arbitration and accredit arbitrators, it remains incompletely implemented. Its accreditation criteria were also criticised for effectively excluding foreign-qualified arbitrators.

bank.q: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is based on:
bank.e: The UNCITRAL Model Law. The New York and Geneva Conventions govern enforcement of foreign awards under Part II.

bank.q: With reference to the structure of the Act, consider the following statements:
s: Part I governs domestic and international commercial arbitration seated in India.
Part II governs enforcement of foreign awards.
Part III governs conciliation, resulting in a binding settlement agreement.
bank.e: All three are correct. Part IV contains supplementary provisions including High Court rule-making powers.

bank.q: Match List I (section) with List II (subject):
pairs: 4. Grounds for setting aside an award
bank.e: Section 5 limits intervention, 16 confers Kompetenz-Kompetenz, 34 sets out setting-aside grounds, and 36 makes awards enforceable as decrees.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about Gayatri Balasamy (2025)?
o: Courts may sever invalid parts of an award
Courts may correct clerical or computational errors
Courts have a general power to modify awards on merits
Article 142 remains available to the Supreme Court
bank.e: There is no general power to modify. The permitted grounds are severability, clerical and computational errors, and post-award interest not complying with the Act.

bank.as: BALCO limited the reach of Indian courts over foreign-seated arbitration.
bank.rs: It held that Part I applies only to arbitrations seated in India.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The 2015 amendment later carved out a limited exception allowing Indian courts to grant interim relief for foreign-seated arbitrations.

bank.q: Consider the following changes made by the 2015 amendment:
s: A twelve-month timeline, extendable by six months.
Narrowing the public policy ground for setting aside.
Creation of the Arbitration Council of India.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 belong to 2015. The Arbitration Council of India came with the 2019 amendment.

bank.q: Which case held that the power under section 11 is judicial rather than administrative?
o: S. B. P. & Co. v. Patel Engineering
bank.e: S. B. P. & Co. v. Patel Engineering (2006), on the nature of the Chief Justice's appointment power.

bank.q: All of the following are identified as problems with Indian arbitration EXCEPT:
o: Absence of any mechanism to enforce awards
bank.e: Enforcement is well provided for — section 36 makes an award enforceable as a decree of the court.

bank.q: Shri Lal Mahal (2013) held that public policy in enforcement proceedings is:
bank.e: Narrower — a deliberate limitation on resisting enforcement of foreign awards.

bank.q: With reference to the conduct of arbitral proceedings, consider the following:
s: The tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure or the Evidence Act.
Interim relief may be sought from both the tribunal and the courts.
An award need not state reasons.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. An award must be in writing, reasoned and signed.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
bank.e: ONGC v. Saw Pipes (2003) → BALCO (2012) → the 2015 amendment → Gayatri Balasamy (2025).
